source_title: Russo makes history with WCL hat-trick as Arsenal cruise to Benfica win
source_excerpt:
Alessia Russo wrote herself into the history books once more as she became the highest English goalscorer in the Women’s Champions League. Her hat-trick gave Arsenal a vital 3-0 win against Benfica to send the Gunners up to second in the league phase table.
“I’m so happy. I think we’ve found a nice dynamic as well with the last two games,” Russo’s manager, Renée Slegers, said. “She’s one of the leaders and she does it her way. She cares for everyone around her and connects well with her teammates. She leads the way as a role model, doing the right things consistently.”
It was a statement performance from the 27-year-old who has shaken off the early-season cobwebs. Her three goals at Meadow Park on Wednesday took her tally up to 10 in her past seven appearances for club and country, hitting a rich vein of form just when Arsenal have needed her most.
It is safe to say Arsenal’s season has yet to fully burst into life. Struggles in front of goal and unforced errors have defined the opening two months but the gritty north London derby win on Saturday did feel like it could be a springboard for momentum.
There was no less pressure coming into this Champions League match against Benfica, another must-win game with Arsenal’s European form mirroring their domestic struggles. A last-ditch win against HB Køge and a heartbreaking draw against Paris FC (in which they surrendered a two‑goal lead) left them fifth in the league phase table before kick-off, with Barcelona and OL Lyonnes looming.
Slegers made three changes to freshen things up. Ona Batlle returned to her more natural right‑back role while the summer signings Élisa De Almeida and Géraldine Reuteler made their full debuts.
Ivan Baptista’s Benfica arrived in confident form on the back of consecutive wins domestically. Slegers was keen to highlight their strong identity pre-match, having had first‑hand experience of their resilience in last year’s league phase. So it proved once more in a first half in which Arsenal dominated, but struggled to break through against a well-structured opposition.
It was the visitors, in fact, who had the best opportunity of the first half hour. Frøya Dorsin was left beating the turf in frustration after spurning a glorious opportunity to catch out a stranded Misa Rodríguez with a lob. It was a moment that jolted Arsenal into life as they upped the tempo and began to rain pressure on Benfica’s goal. First Olivia Smith set up Russo for a low shot that went narrowly wide before Smith herself forced Lena Pauels into a fine save.
Arsenal found their breakthrough just before half-time when Russo produced a sublime finish after a well‑worked move down the left.
It was like a switch had flipped for Arsenal after the break as they exuded confidence, zipping the ball around the turf with increasing ease. Smith looked more and more comfortable in her central role while Caitlin Foord came alive down the left, the latter denied a clear shot by a superb last-ditch challenge.
The conductor behind them all was Russo as she pressed and stretched the play to her tune. The captain on the night was at the heart of things once more as the hosts doubled their lead, rising high to glance home a corner. She completed her hat-trick shortly afterwards, converting from the spot after Foord was brought down by Catarina Amado.
Chelsea maintained their strong start to this year’s Women’s Champions League campaign as second-half goals from Ellie Carpenter [pictured, centre] and Kadeisha Buchanan secured a 2-0 win over Roma at Plough Lane.
After a goalless first half, substitute Carpenter combined with Wieke Kaptein to open the scoring in the 51st minute. The Australian made a powerful run, found Kaptein and then met her cross from the right with a low shot which took a deflection off Roma defender Winonah Heatley before going in.
Central defender Buchanan wrapped up the win in the 89th minute, heading home to ensure a second win in three European matches for Sonia Bompastor’s unbeaten team. Roma were left to rue chances missed by Maya Doms and Alayah Pilgrim as they extended their scoreless Champions League start to three games.
'I’m pleased with the fact we scored really early in the second half. We could probably have killed the game a little bit earlier,' said the Chelsea head coach, Sonia Bompastor. 'It’s important for us in these games to be able to be clinical and ruthless as early as possible. But we find different ways to impose ourselves in the game and to score goals. So it’s good.'
Bayern Munich fought back from two goals down to draw 2-2 against Real Madrid and preserve their unbeaten home record in the pre-knockout phase. Last season’s semi-finalists have now not lost any of their 17 home games in the group stage or league phase thanks to Momoko Tanikawa's second-half equaliser.
Athenea del Castillo pounced from Linda Caicedo’s cross in the seventh minute, before Lineth Beerensteyn headed in from close range to double Madrid’s lead midway through the first half. Edna Imade nodded in to reduce the deficit on the half-hour and Tanikawa levelled soon after the restart, before Sophie Proost hit the post for Bayern in stoppage time.
Eight-time champions Lyonnes cruised to an emphatic 6-0 home victory over Internazionale , with Marie-Antoinette Katoto scoring twice before Lily Yohannes made it three on the hour mark. Vicki Bècho came off the bench shortly after and hit a hat-trick as the French giants went top of the table on goal difference.
Swiss side Servette claimed a historic maiden Champions League win at the ninth attempt as they brushed aside OH Leuven 5-1 in Geneva. Paola Hernández and Gloria Marinelli both struck twice to leave the Belgian champions winless so far in this season’s league phase. Press Association
It was a finish that marked the 200th goal of Slegers’s tenure and one that further eases the pressure on the head coach. With every minute that passed the hosts looked increasingly like themselves and could have added more to their tally.
“It looks like there is something off our shoulders,” Slegers said. “We were playing like us tonight and I am so happy. The players enjoyed themselves – they connected, they expressed themselves and they played with intensity. We backed the last performance up. We need to do it again at the weekend.”
There will no doubt be sterner tests to come in Europe, more immediately away to Barcelona in a fortnight’s time, but this was a victory that signified something more important than just climbing up the Champions League table.
hi_body:
एलिसिया रूसो महिला चैंपियंस लीग के इतिहास में सबसे ज्यादा गोल करने वाली अंग्रेजी खिलाड़ी बन गई हैं। उन्होंने मीडो पार्क में बेनफिका के खिलाफ आर्सेनल की 3-0 की जीत में शानदार हैट्रिक दर्ज की। इस जीत के साथ आर्सेनल टूर्नामेंट की लीग तालिका में दूसरे स्थान पर पहुंच गया है।

## मैच का सारांश
*   **आर्सेनल बनाम बेनफिका:** आर्सेनल ने 3-0 से महत्वपूर्ण जीत हासिल की।
*   **मुख्य खिलाड़ी:** एलिसिया रूसो ने टीम के लिए तीनों गोल किए।
*   **टूर्नामेंट की स्थिति:** आर्सेनल लीग तालिका में अब दूसरे पायदान पर है।

पहले हाफ में कड़े मुकाबले के बाद, रूसो ने हाफ-टाइम से ठीक पहले गोल करके खाता खोला। दूसरे हाफ में उनका प्रदर्शन और निखर कर सामने आया, जहां उन्होंने एक कॉर्नर किक पर हेडर से गोल किया और कैटलिन फूर्ड के खिलाफ हुए फाउल के बाद मिली पेनल्टी को गोल में बदलकर अपनी हैट्रिक पूरी की। आर्सेनल की मैनेजर रेनी स्लेजर्स ने रूसो के नेतृत्व की सराहना की। उन्होंने कहा कि यह जीत टीम के आत्मविश्वास के लिए बहुत जरूरी थी, क्योंकि उन्हें आगामी मैचों में बार्सिलोना जैसी मजबूत टीमों का सामना करना है।

## अन्य यूरोपीय मैच परिणाम
महिला चैंपियंस लीग के अन्य मैचों के परिणाम निम्नलिखित रहे:
*   **चेल्सी:** एली कारपेंटर और कदीशा बुकानन के गोलों की बदौलत रोमा को 2-0 से हराया।
*   **बायर्न म्यूनिख:** दो गोल से पिछड़ने के बाद रियल मैड्रिड के साथ 2-2 से ड्रॉ खेला।
*   **ल्योन:** विक्की बेचो की हैट्रिक की मदद से इंटरनेजियोनेल को 6-0 से मात दी।
*   **सर्वेट:** ओएच ल्यूवेन को 5-1 से हराकर चैंपियंस लीग में अपनी पहली जीत दर्ज की।

आर्सेनल का बेनफिका के खिलाफ प्रदर्शन उनके घरेलू मैचों की तुलना में काफी बेहतर रहा। आधिकारिक यूईएफए (UEFA) पोर्टल पर परिणामों और अंकों की तालिका की पुष्टि की जा सकती है।

hi_meta: एलिसिया रूसो ने चैंपियंस लीग में हैट्रिक लगाकर इतिहास रचा। आर्सेनल ने बेनफिका को 3-0 से हराकर लीग तालिका में दूसरा स्थान हासिल किया।
en_body:
Alessia Russo has become the highest-scoring English player in the history of the Women’s Champions League following her hat-trick in Arsenal’s 3-0 victory over Benfica at Meadow Park. The win propels the Gunners to second place in the tournament's league phase standings.

## Match Overview
*   **Arsenal vs. Benfica:** Arsenal secured a crucial 3-0 win.
*   **Key Performer:** Alessia Russo netted all three goals for the home side.
*   **Tournament Status:** Arsenal now sits second in the league phase table.

After a tightly contested first half, Russo opened the scoring just before the break. Her performance continued to intensify in the second half, where she headed in a corner and successfully converted a penalty following a foul on teammate Caitlin Foord. Arsenal manager Renée Slegers praised Russo’s leadership and impact, noting that the victory represents a significant boost in confidence for the squad as they prepare for future challenges, including a forthcoming away match against Barcelona.

## Broader European Results
Other fixtures in the Women’s Champions League also saw notable outcomes:
*   **Chelsea:** Secured a 2-0 win against Roma with goals from Ellie Carpenter and Kadeisha Buchanan.
*   **Bayern Munich:** Fought back from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Real Madrid.
*   **Lyon:** Defeated Internazionale 6-0, led by a hat-trick from substitute Vicki Bècho.
*   **Servette:** Achieved their first-ever Champions League victory by beating OH Leuven 5-1.

Arsenal’s performance against Benfica was marked by a shift in momentum, with the team displaying greater cohesion compared to their recent domestic struggles. Fans can verify these results and standings through official UEFA competition portals.
en_title: Alessia Russo Makes History with Champions League Hat-Trick as Arsenal Defeat Benfica
